clue.text: Journey between landings

explanation.surface: A trip made somewhere between touching down at airports.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a trip by air, and also the run of stairs climbing from one floor landing to the next.

clue.text: Left grannie perplexedly gaining skill

indicators.note: a perplexed granny is muddled, so the letters of the word grannie are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a confused grandmother while picking up a new ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' gives the single opening letter by the usual abbreviation; 'perplexedly' then scrambles the grandmother word, a nonstandard spelling of granny, to supply the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acquiring knowledge or ability through study is the process of education, so gaining skill describes it.

clue.text: Tip guy with artist out, not suddenly initially

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order and rearranged
not means the following letter is left out of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word suddenly

explanation.surface: Advice to tip a man once a painter has abruptly left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not suddenly initially' removes S from ARTIST, leaving ARTIT; 'out' then rearranges GUY with ARTIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gratuity is money given to a waiter or driver in thanks for service, which is what a tip is.

clue.text: Lady repeatedly included new sound of trumpet

indicators.note: included means the abbreviation for new is placed within the doubled name
repeatedly says the lady's name is written down twice in a row

parts.note: Tara is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman kept including something fresh in a trumpet call.
explanation.walkthrough: TARA twice gives TARATARA; 'included' puts N between the two copies.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarantara is an imitative word for a fanfare or blast on a bugle or horn.

clue.text: Caribbean country or less than half of another

explanation.surface: A Caribbean nation which is only a fraction of a neighbouring state.
explanation.walkthrough: The other country is the Dominican Republic: its first eight letters, fewer than half of its seventeen, spell this island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominica is an island nation in the Lesser Antilles, and its name forms the opening portion of the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: Tactful body for the most part can be found residing in another country

definitions.text: can be found residing in another country

parts.note: diplomatic means tactful and discreet

indicators.note: for the most part means nearly all of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a corpse is a dead body

explanation.surface: A discreet group of people who mostly live abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' cuts the final E from CORPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The ambassadors and embassy staff of a nation are posted to and live in foreign capitals.

clue.text: Mistakenly coming from liner, Rory appeared

indicators.note: coming from says the letters emerge from inside the words liner and Rory

explanation.surface: Rory turned up on an ocean liner by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something by mistake is to act wrongly, so the phrase works as an adverb of error.

clue.text: Travelling at the front

explanation.surface: Journeying while leading the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding in a vehicle such as a van means travelling, and the van, short for vanguard, is the leading position.

clue.text: Animal or insect to make a bolt

parts.note: an ant is a common insect
to elope is to run off secretly to marry, making a bolt for it

explanation.surface: Which creature would run off: a beast or a bug?
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a bolt' suggests fixing a door; here it means dashing away.
explanation.definitionFit: An antelope is a swift, horned grazing mammal of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Unintentional use of wrong words whilst ripping polar map

indicators.note: ripping tears the map apart, so the letters of polar map are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone garbles their speech while tearing up a chart of the Arctic.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Malaprop, a character in Sheridan's play The Rivals, comically misused similar-sounding words, so her name became a term for the slip.

clue.text: Make off hastily to play one's drum

explanation.surface: Run away in a hurry to bang on percussion.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang order means scram, and literally to strike a drum is to play it.

clue.text: Finish union trouble outside with insinuation

indicators.note: outside means the shuffled letters go around the word meaning finish
trouble stirs up the word union so that its letters are shuffled

parts.note: end means finish

explanation.surface: Bringing industrial strife to a close by hinting at things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish' looks like a verb opening a command; it simply supplies the letters that sit within the jumbled trade-union word, which 'trouble' rearranges as INNUO.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect, usually suggestive or disparaging, hint.

clue.text: Gold to distribute during trial

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
to deal is to hand out, as with cards

explanation.surface: Gold is to be shared out in the middle of a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or testing experience, and historically a trial by fire or water.

clue.text: Brewer?

parts.note: suggests a person making beer, but it is someone who makes a pot of the hot drink

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brews a pot of leaves in hot water is producing the drink from them.

clue.text: Lasting quality put to the test

definitions.text: Lasting quality put to the test

parts.words: Lasting quality put to the test
parts.note: the staying power that is examined in a long, gruelling contest such as a marathon

explanation.surface: A durable characteristic being examined.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina, the ability to keep going, is what a gruelling test of that kind measures.

clue.text: Hideous sort of customer?

explanation.surface: What kind of shopper is frightful?
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly means unpleasant to look at, and a nasty, dangerous person is called an ugly customer.

clue.text: Likely to be held up when rain stops play

definitions.text: Likely to be held up when rain stops play

parts.words: Likely to be held up when rain stops play
parts.note: sounds like a delayed cricket match, but means the thing raised over spectators' heads in a shower

explanation.definitionFit: A brolly is raised overhead to keep off the wet when a shower halts a cricket match.

clue.text: Dial in a relaxed way!

parts.note: the word dial read from end to start becomes laid, so it is laid in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: Phone someone casually.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the word Dial shows LAID turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: Being easygoing and calm, unhurried, is how the phrase describes manner.

clue.text: Singular occasion in prison cell

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the words prison cell

explanation.surface: A unique event inside a jail cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done on a single occasion happens one time only.

clue.text: Following intended route while playing golf

explanation.surface: Keeping to the planned path during a round on the links.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping to plan means staying on track, and a golfer during a round is out on the links.

clue.text: One in cool air over squid

indicators.note: in means the letter for one goes inside the word for cool

parts.note: calm means cool and unflustered
A means one, as in a single item

indicators.note: over signals that the word air is turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: A single creature in the chilly breeze above the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' gives A here rather than I; 'over' works as an anagram signal, turning the breeze word into ARI rather than reversing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is the Italian-derived menu name for squid served as food.

clue.text: Herb went to river in new town

parts.note: basil is a culinary herb
the Don is a river in Yorkshire, and in Russia

explanation.surface: A herb was taken to a river in a recently built town.
explanation.walkthrough: BASILDON is a town in Essex, England, built after 1949 as one of Britain's planned new towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Basildon was one of the planned settlements created under Britain's post-war programme to rehouse Londoners.

clue.text: Everyone in favour that it should be blown up

indicators.note: in means the word for everyone is placed inside the word for favour

parts.note: a boon is a favour or blessing
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everybody supports the idea that something ought to be destroyed by explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: A party toy made of rubber is inflated with air before use.

clue.text: Screen poser

explanation.surface: A display that puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse sieve for sifting soil is called by this name, and a puzzling question is also one.

clue.text: Military officer who is non-spiritual losing energy

indicators.note: losing says a letter drops out of the word meaning non-spiritual

parts.note: corporeal means bodily, of the flesh rather than the spirit
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A soldier who is earthly and lacks vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes the E out of CORPOREAL. A corporal is strictly a non-commissioned officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporal is a rank in the army just above lance corporal, an NCO in command of a section.

clue.text: Go ahead, like a well controlled dog

explanation.surface: Carry on, just as an obedient pet would.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide others forward is to go first, and an obedient dog walks on its leash.

clue.text: Way round town

parts.note: reads like directions across a town, but means a road circling it to bypass the centre

explanation.definitionFit: A circular bypass carries traffic around the edge of a town.

clue.text: Ranks as a new state

indicators.note: new means the letters of ranks as a are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Lines up as a fresh political unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is one of the fifty US states, in the south.

clue.text: Drop it in a wink

parts.note: sounds like doing something instantly, but describes the fold of skin lowered over the eye when winking

explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin that covers the eye is lowered briefly when one winks.
